decisions: **D1 (plan-holds-ranges)**: the ranges live in `intent.md` under `## Build ranges`, right after `## Build order`, *because* the plan is already the tracked document the skills edit and the parser reads, which is why plumbbob [D86 (build-order)](https://github.com/robmclarty/plumbbob/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#d86) put the sequence there, and all three hand-written sections already sit in a plan.

**D2 (range-grammar)**: a range is one numbered item, `` `/plumbbob:build 6-9`, **stop:** ``, with an optional `- model:` sub-line and any other sub-line (a `- note:` on what to watch for) left to the reader, *because* the Steps grammar already reads this way, an item wraps where a table row of prose runs off the screen, and the item's number is the handle the card counts by.

**D3 (form-says-where)**: the command's form says where a range stops: a bare `N` builds step N to its pause, so its stop is a call made before the step lands, and a range lands every step it names and stops at the boundary after the last, so its stop is a review of what landed, *because* that is what the two forms already do (plumbbob [D85 (range-top-lands)](https://github.com/robmclarty/plumbbob/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#d85)), so a stop needs no kind of its own.

**D4 (advice-not-grant)**: a range in the section grants nothing, and the human still types the command, *because* a grant comes only from the human's literal prompt (plumbbob [D65 (human-typed-grants)](https://github.com/robmclarty/plumbbob/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#d65)), and a line the model can edit would be a grant the model could forge (plumbbob [D67 (auto-not-a-grant)](https://github.com/robmclarty/plumbbob/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#d67)).

**D5 (one-grammar)**: the section's command and the grant the hook mints from a typed range are read by one parser, *because* a card that reads a range one way while the hook reads it another would suggest a command that does something else.

**D6 (state-is-derived)**: a range's progress is read from its steps' boxes and never stored: done when every step it names is `[x]`, in progress when it holds the next undone step in build order, *because* the boxes are already the truth, and a second copy of a fact is one more thing to drift.

**D7 (plan-places-stops)**: the plan decides where ranges stop and the CLI never does: a range ends where a human call is due (a decision the plan leaves open, a review before later steps build on what landed, or something only the human can do, such as a push, a live key, or spending money) and nowhere else, *because* where a call falls is judgment, and all three hand-written sections cut at exactly those points.

**D8 (model-declared)**: a range's model is what its own `- model:` line says, never computed from its steps, *because* a ranking of model names in code goes stale with the next release, the same reason tokens and cost stay out of the `spent` row.

**D9 (informative-only)**: each new card and dashboard line renders only when the plan declares ranges and the line says something the card does not already hold, *because* a reminder that repeats what is on screen is noise (plumbbob [D86 (build-order)](https://github.com/robmclarty/plumbbob/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#d86) made the same call for its line), and a plan without the section has to render exactly as it does today.

**D10 (drift-reported)**: a range the plan has outgrown is reported and never rewritten by the CLI: one naming a step the plan lacks, a step two ranges both name, an undone step no range names, or an undone step outside a range that the build order places between two of the range's own; the dashboard names it, `recover` names one that points at a step the plan lacks (as it does for the build order), and the card suggests no command for it, *because* only the human knows where the stop belongs now, and a suggested command that halts early is the failure this build exists to remove.

**D11 (notice-not-turn)**: a background job's completion notice is not a human turn: for a prompt step 1's rule marks as a notice, the prompt hook leaves `TURN` and `GRANT` as they were and emits no nudge, *because* the latch reads `TURN` passing a step's entry stamp as its only sign that a human answered, and two ranges this week lost their grant to a Stryker run's notice (settles [Q1 (notice-not-turn)](#q1)).

**D12 (step-list-grants)**: a range may list its steps, numbers and spans joined by commas (`20,5-9`); the hook mints exactly that set, the latch lands only its members, and a plain `N-M` grants exactly N through M, *because* the set is fixed by what the human typed, so no later edit to the build order can widen it, where reading `N-M` along the build order would let the model widen a grant by reordering the plan (settles [Q2 (step-list-grants)](#q2)).

**D13 (card-shape)**: the note beneath Next Up opens with the range holding the step Next Up names and the command that runs what is left of it (`· range 3 of 5: /plumbbob:build 6-9`), or says the range needs a re-cut, and why, when [D10 (drift-reported)](#d10) flags it; a `**Stop**: Range 3 of 5 landed - ` part sits between the advisories and Next Up on the boundary where a landing range's last step lands, and nowhere else; and the dashboard lists the ranges under the steps (`ranges 2 of 5 done`, with ✓ and ▸), a drift row per flagged range, and a `next →` that names the range's command, *because* those are the two questions the human brings to a boundary, what to type next and why the build stopped, and a bare range's stop is its own pause, where the injected dashboard already puts the stop text in front of the model writing the recommendation (settles [Q3 (card-shape)](#q3); the exact strings are step 5's).

**D14 (auto-and-stops)**: under `--auto`, a step the ranges name as a bare range is built to its pause and halts there at the decision tier, with `plumbbob build` saying so as it enters the step; a review stop is run through, a typed range stays as typed, and the halt is the build notice's and the skill's, never the latch's, *because* a plan that reserves a call for the human should not have it made by a flag typed for speed, a review can wait for the end of the run, and the ranges are advice under [D4 (advice-not-grant)](#d4) (settles [Q4 (auto-and-stops)](#q4)).

**D15 (notice-clears-relay)**: a notice also clears `RELAY`, through a `clearRelay` beside `clearPause` in `src/lib/sidecar.ts`, *because* the ending in it was judged when its own turn ended, a hold mark would carry forward within the `TURN` (`writeRelay`, `src/lib/sidecar.ts:728`) and wave through any ending printed after the notice, and a fresh record is checked as usual (settles [Q5 (notice-and-relay)](#q5)).

**D16 (list-reading)**: once any token in the argument run carries a comma or a dash, every number and span in the run joins one set, and bare numbers alone mint nothing; a range starts at its first undone step in build order, however it is written; and the card writes a list in build order (`20,5-9`, `48-51,76,52-57`), *because* `20, 5-9` with a space reads today as `range 9`, which refuses the range's first step, and a set has no order of its own, so the build order has to supply it (settles [Q6 (list-reading)](#q6)).

**D17 (range-model)**: while the note suggests a range, the bold model in Next Up's bracket is the range's and the note names no model; otherwise the bracket keeps the step's, *because* the range's model is the `/model` the human picks before typing it, and a range's first step is often not its hardest (settles [Q7 (range-model)](#q7)).

**D18 (scaffold-range)**: step 5's spec fixes the template's placeholder range; an item whose command or stop still holds a `<...>` fill-in reads as scaffold, neither a range nor a report; and [D10 (drift-reported)](#d10)'s coverage check runs only once at least one real range parses, *because* a fresh build would otherwise warn on its dashboard and flag every step, and plumbbob [D77 (placeholder-uncounted)](https://github.com/robmclarty/plumbbob/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#d77) settled the same case for the scaffolded question (settles [Q8 (scaffold-range)](#q8)).
constraints: **C1 (no-new-deps)**: no new dependency of any kind.
**C2 (hooks-never-wedge)**: every hook path (`turn`, `relay`) still exits 0 and degrades to no output on any failure.
**C3 (records-stay-put)**: no file in another build's folder is edited, here or in another repo; a plan written before this build keeps parsing as no ranges.

**C4 (spec-first)**: a change to a turn's shape lands in `docs/presentation.md` before the code that renders it, per plumbbob [D80 (cli-renders-model-relays)](https://github.com/robmclarty/plumbbob/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#d80).
**C5 (no-release)**: no version bump and no CHANGELOG entry; the release is cut by hand with `/version`.
**C6 (temp-repo-dogfood)**: hand-run checks use `node src/cli.ts` in a `mktemp -d` repo, never a stale `dist/` and never this repo's live session.

**C7 (house-voice)**: authored prose follows `docs/voice/` with no em-dash (plumbbob [D78 (em-dash-ban)](https://github.com/robmclarty/plumbbob/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#d78)), relayed CLI strings keep theirs, and every citation carries its slug (plumbbob [D74 (glossed-citations)](https://github.com/robmclarty/plumbbob/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#d74)).

**C8 (old-grants-land)**: the latch keeps honoring a `range M` grant, ceiling and all, *because* this repo's own prompt hook is the installed plugin's until a release, and this build's ranges have to land while it runs.
**C9 (numbers-for-life)**: nothing renumbers a step, and a range names plan numbers (plumbbob [D86 (build-order)](https://github.com/robmclarty/plumbbob/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#d86)).
